# UMC capital and claims: dated June 30, 2026 study

Research cutoff: October 19, 2026. This is a historical capital bridge with a separate subsequent-events overlay. It is not a current October balance sheet or a complete fair-value target.

## The denominator is ordinary shares, with five ordinary shares per ADS

The June anchor has 12,576,984,870 issued ordinary shares and 30,551,000 treasury shares, leaving 12,546,433,870 ordinary shares outstanding, or 2,509,286,774 economic ADS equivalents. The actual ADS float was only 147,069,766 receipts, representing 735,348,830 ordinary shares. Dividing total company equity by that receipt float would dramatically overstate per-ADS value. The exact treasury count is established by the June 29 buyback-completion announcement, not merely the interim report's rounded table. Treasury shares were bought for employee transfer and are not permanently retired.

Sources: [May capital registration](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526220535/umc-ex99.htm), [June buyback completion](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526286731/umc-ex99_1.htm), [issuer June ADS count](https://www.umc.com/en/Html/faqs), [interim report, Note 6(19)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm).

Restricted employee shares are issued before vesting and already included in issued share capital. Adding the diluted-EPS restricted-share adjustment to issued shares less treasury would count those shares twice. The Q2 basic and diluted weighted averages also differ from the point-in-time denominator. A subsequent 6,890,971-share restricted-stock cancellation reduced outstanding shares to 12,539,542,899 when registered on August 10. The February25 board notice specifies a maximum67m new restricted shares, subsequently approved at the May AGM. They vest33%/33%/34% after two, three and four years subject to service and performance. This authorization is separate from already-issued awards. Actual issuance timing remains unverified. The company estimated NT$3.867771bn total compensation over2026–2030 under its stated assumptions; that estimate is neither a cash liability nor evidence of actual June issuance. Existing compensation cost and future award uncertainty should remain in the model; a cash-flow SBC addback is not inherently free cash.

Sources: [interim report, Notes 6(20), 6(27)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm), [August registration](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526350180/umc-ex99.htm), [AGM resolutions](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526240337/umc-ex99.htm), [new restricted-share terms](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526068351/umc-ex99.htm).

## Separate excess cash from funding already spoken for

Cash and equivalents were NT$124.706465bn. Another NT$22.135867bn consisted of time deposits with original maturities beyond three months. Their accessibility before maturity and geographic availability are not fully established. The deposits should therefore be displayed separately rather than silently reclassified as same-day cash.

Financial debt was NT$57.532565bn carrying value. A principal/contractual-redemption proxy is NT$57.557436bn before NT$24.871m of bond discounts. This includes NT$39.1bn domestic bond face, NT$17.892245bn total bank loans, and NT$565.191m contractual TWD-equivalent redemption for the residual Novatek exchangeable bond. That older bond exchanges into Novatek shares, not newly issued UMC shares. Its residual US$20.9m principal is inferred from the original US$400m, less US$187.1m repurchased and US$192m exchanged. Applying the 96.92% redemption factor and fixed 27.902 TWD/USD produces NT$565.190725m, reconciling the reported amount. It matured July 7, 2026; the reviewed subsequent SEC set does not separately confirm its final cash settlement.

The NT$32.704164bn dividend payable was already a June liability. Ordinary shareholders' cash payment date was July 30; ADS holders' payment date was August 6. A June ex-declared-distribution study can subtract this claim once. A later cash roll-forward can instead subtract the paid cash. It cannot do both. The dividend's record dates and the period of earnings from which it was declared are not cash-payment dates.

Sources: [interim statements, Notes 6(1), 6(4), 6(11), 6(13), 6(14), 6(19)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm), [dividend declaration and ordinary payment schedule](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526278424/umc-ex99.htm), [ADS payment schedule](https://www.umc.com/en/IR_Stock/dividend_information).

## Customer funding and leases require one consistent treatment

Guarantee deposits total NT$40.674252bn including the current portion, and mainly represent capacity-reservation deposits. Contractual maturity disclosure places NT$0.629206bn within one year, NT$19.081785bn in years two to three, NT$18.178491bn in years four to five, and NT$2.784770bn thereafter. The current balance derived from the balance sheet differs from the first bucket by NT$1,000 because of rounding. These are substantial customer funding obligations. The public notes do not establish the complete refund, offset or cancellation mechanics of each contract.

A conservative framework can deduct the full deposit claim from equity and reserve the same money from available liquidity. Future refunds then draw on that reserved pool; they are not another full deduction from FCFF. Alternatively, a properly specified operating-working-capital model could include their runoff. Mixing those approaches double-counts the obligation. Contract liabilities and refund liabilities are separate balance-sheet lines and should not be silently merged with the guarantee deposits.

For leases, either subtract the lease liability with a financing-consistent FCFF, or charge total future lease cash as an operating cash cost, add back the corresponding right-of-use depreciation, and avoid another lease-PV deduction. The June lease liability was NT$5.917316bn; H1 principal payments were NT$420.478m and recognized lease interest NT$93.065m. Expense is not necessarily cash interest paid.

Source: [interim report, Notes 6(9), 6(24), 6(28), 12(5)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm).

## Operating earnings and investment wealth are different questions

Q2 operating income was NT$14.949990bn, while parent net income was NT$42.259962bn. The gap contains NT$23.605970bn of equity-method profit and NT$6.067021bn of fair-value gains. Both sit outside foundry operating FCFF. The H1 associate contribution was heavily concentrated in investment-holding affiliates: Hsun Chieh Investment contributed NT$21.209726bn and Yann Yuan NT$2.584048bn. This establishes investment exposure, but does not establish that every dollar was one identifiable, nonrecurring disposal. A safe characterization is volatile nonoperating investment-derived profit whose Q2 level should not be capitalized as recurring foundry earnings.

The Novatek bond exchange is different again. NT$6.018202bn of shares were derecognized, and NT$4.142004bn of cumulative FVOCI gains moved to retained earnings. That transfer did not create the Q2 income-statement profit and was not a cash sale to add to liquidity.

Direct FVTPL assets were NT$27.672121bn and direct FVOCI assets NT$23.249916bn. These exclude equity-method associates. Of the combined NT$50.922037bn, NT$29.256260bn is Level 1, NT$25.320m Level 2 and NT$21.640457bn Level 3. Level 3 contains valuation judgment and limited marketability; it should not be called liquid cash.

Equity-method holdings have NT$96.474468bn carrying value. The listed trio, SIS, Faraday and Unimicron, has exact aggregate carrying value NT$30.031474bn; the report separately gives rounded quoted fair value NT$232.714bn. The remaining NT$66.442994bn is unlisted-associate carrying value, not fair value. Quoted stakes may still face taxes, transaction costs, market impact, strategic restrictions and price changes. No blanket book-to-fair-value conversion is justified.

Circular ownership also matters: Hsun Chieh, SIS, Yann Yuan and Unimicron hold UMC shares. A portfolio addback must remove or solve that recursive UMC exposure rather than count it as an independent outside asset. For an operating-only study, assigning all nonoperating equity investments zero incremental value while excluding their earnings and taking no circular-share denominator benefit is internally simple. It is an exclusion convention, not a finding that those investments are worthless. The result must be labelled an operating-value study with omitted economic assets, not a complete fair-value target.

Source: [interim report, Notes 6(3), 6(7), 6(24), 12(7), Attachments 4 and 7](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm).

## Taxes and minority claims cannot be reduced to book-value shortcuts

Current tax payable of NT$5.216199bn can be reserved as a prior-period cash claim if future cash taxes and working-capital runoff do not already include it. The June deferred tax liability is NT$13.498249bn and deferred tax asset NT$9.971653bn. Their current-period operating-versus-investment breakdown was not resolved from the interim disclosure. Deducting all deferred tax liabilities while using cash-tax FCFF can double-count timing differences. Likewise, deferred tax assets are not immediately spendable cash.

The renewed Taiwan-Singapore tax agreement generated a reported NT$1.947bn increase in deferred tax assets, while the company warned that the future tax-sparing phaseout could raise its effective tax rate. This makes a mechanically annualized H1 reported tax rate especially weak. NCI book value was only NT$4.051m, but book value is not an appraisal of the minority claim. Any deliberately conservative reserve, such as NT$100m, is an analyst assumption and should be labelled accordingly.

Source: [interim report, balance sheet and Note 6(26)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm).

## Post-June financing changes the current picture

Two domestic convertible programs authorized June 3 had face limits of NT$12bn and NT$4bn. Cash receipts of NT$12.12bn and NT$4.792798780bn were subsequently confirmed, with initial conversion prices NT$146 and NT$130.7. Proceeds include issue premiums and are not interchangeable with principal or the dilution numerator. A conditional full-face conversion produces about 112.796m ordinary shares in total. Final domestic put/call terms were not established from the reviewed SEC notices.

The amended October 5 announcement prices another US$1.8bn in two equal overseas convertible tranches, with October 13 scheduled issuance. Tranche A matures October 2031 but has holder puts in October 2027 and October 2029. Tranche B matures April 2028. Initial conversion prices are NT$202.06 and NT$179.19, with fixed FX of 31.753 TWD/USD. The second price is mistakenly labelled “Tranche A” in the amended English notice, so identifying it as B is a contextual inference pending an indenture or exchange confirmation. The announced overseas full-conversion increment is approximately 300.915m shares. The reviewed SEC set does not separately establish final cash receipt. A current valuation must consider settlement, future capex, the earliest put and conditional dilution; simply adding gross proceeds to June cash overstates owner wealth.

Sources: [June authorizations](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526254481/umc-ex99.htm), [first domestic pricing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526324785/umc-ex99.htm), [first receipt](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526333718/umc-ex99_1.htm), [second pricing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526350180/umc-ex99.htm), [second receipt](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526379275/umc-ex99_1.htm), [amended overseas pricing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526413417/umc-ex99_1.htm).

## Expansion needs a dated funding plan

At June 30, unrecognized construction commitments were approximately NT$12bn and unrecognized IP/royalty/development commitments NT$1.4bn. Cash capex should include unpaid prior additions as well as future construction and equipment; do not subtract a commitment again when it is already included in forecast cash spending. The July 29 NT$148.68bn phased expansion authorization and US$2bn 2026 capex guidance are not two wholly incremental immediate cash liabilities. A separate NT$1.7bn maximum TGVest fund commitment is payable through capital calls.

The Intel 12nm collaboration uses Intel's established US manufacturing footprint, but that does not establish a zero-capital, zero-risk project for UMC. The 2025 20-F explicitly identifies additional US costs and investment, implementation and control risks, and possible failure to earn the expected returns. It anticipates production in 2027. No separately quantified, binding UMC cash-contribution schedule was established, so this remains a scenario funding requirement rather than an invented exact commitment.

Sources: [June commitments](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm), [July expansion and fund authorization](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322027/umc-ex99.htm), [2025 20-F, Intel collaboration and risk factors](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526193757/d91630d20f.htm).

## FX policy

Use the separately verified June 30 CBC spot rate of 31.837 TWD/USD for the June-anchored study. The latest prior-session CBC close at the October research cutoff was 32.338 on October 16. That is a different dated observation, not a replacement for the June anchor. EPS translation averages and the convertibles' fixed contractual FX have different purposes and must not be used as valuation spot FX.

Source: [CBC daily closing rates](https://www.cbc.gov.tw/en/lp-700-2.html); June observation is frozen in the parent package's FX record.

## Legacy settlement reserves

June liabilities also include NT$833.593m net defined-benefit pension obligations and provisions of NT$926.028m for decommissioning, NT$105.949m for onerous contracts, and NT$41.971m for carbon fees. The combined NT$1,907.541m can be shown as a conservative opening settlement reserve only to the extent future cash flows do not already pay these obligations. Normal pension service costs do not automatically repay a past-service deficit. Ordinary growth capex does not automatically cover end-of-life restoration. Onerous-contract costs may already be embedded in operating forecasts, and accrued carbon fees may already run through working capital. Reserve each once, with a documented mapping. Source: [interim balance sheet and Notes6(15),6(18)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm).
